text_fidelity_a:
ADORA Baby Doll Stroller with Color Changing Sunny Days Print, Fits Up to 18 Inch Baby Dolls 3 stars

This stroller is very cute, and it is nice that it is in gender-neutral colors, so that boy children as well as girl children can enjoy this stroller. It can be used not just to hold baby dolls, but also stuffed animals.

This toy stroller resembles a typical human-baby, umbrella stroller in design and functionality. The difference between this and a real stroller, though, other than the miniature sizing, is that it is not sturdy. Therefore, there is a safety element in that your child may easily push or lean harder on its handles than it is built to withstand, and end up tripping and falling on top of or tumbling headfirst over it. If you have stairs in your house, this in particular could lead to a dangerous injury.

A major factor contributing to this flimsiness issue is the fact that the wheels are not at all strong and, overall, this toy is very cheaply made. It is certainly not constructed to stand up to the rather rugged treatment a toddler or preschooler would give to a toy like this.

In short, this doll stroller is certainly not a case of, "You get what you pay for." Because of the expensive price of this and all other Adora doll accessories, you'd think you'd be getting something really sturdy and long-lasting. Unfortunately, that is not the case with this stroller.
text_fidelity_b: ADORA Baby Doll Stroller with Color Changing Sunny Days Print, Fits Up to 18 Inch Baby Dolls

text_fidelity_a:
Adora My Cuddle & Coo Baby “Cuppy Cake” - Touch Activated Doll with 5 Sounds: She Cries, Coos, Giggles, Kisses Back & Says Momma Just like I had thought before actually receiving this, you are probably thinking that this is a hefty pricetag for a doll that doesn't even have the American Girl logo attached to it... well, move over Pleasant Company (yeah, I said it), because Adora is a new generation of dolls that are not only kid approved (my girls, ages ranging from 6-10, all love their Adora dolls) but it is also parent/caregiver/teacher approved (I would know, as I'm technically all 3, haha). My girls love this doll because she's so cuddly and lifelike, and I love her because I have spent some time actually researching the Adora company... and let me just say THANK YOU for finally coming out with a line of dolls that are crafted from SAFE and nontoxic materials! No more feeling that tiny pang of worry ("mom guilt" lol) whenever my daughter is snuggled up with her doll. I love the peace of mind that comes from knowing the dolls arms, legs, and face are made of vinyl and are BPA free. Finally, a toy company with ethics!

Many of Adoras dolls are machine washable (this particular one has electronics and therefore is not, so care must be taken when wiping the vinyl parts and perhaps spraying a safe vinegar solution on the dolls plush core to keep clean and fresh). Honestly, I can't really comment on the electronic aspect of this doll, as I turned off that feature pretty early (i think it encourages better open-ended imaginative play that way... not to mention less annoying for cranky mommies lol). So you'll have to check other reviews for better details on that function.

All in all, yes, this is not a cheap doll. But in my humble opinion, you are getting a lot of value for your money with this doll. The brand has less expensive plush options too that are just as adorable, less expensive, and even machine washable (we have one and I'll be doing a review soon). The Adora line has a wide selection of dolls and accessories too by the way. I'm actually excited to buy some accessories because I feel like they are very competitively priced and plus it feels good to support such an ethical company that brings so much joy to children.

Grandparents, this is a gift that will not only make you the favorite grandparent, but will also please even the pickiest of health-conscious daughter-in-laws lol.

Two thumbs up for Adora!!
text_fidelity_b: Adora My Cuddle & Coo Baby “Cuppy Cake” - Touch Activated Doll with 5 Sounds: She Cries, Coos, Giggles, Kisses Back & Says Momma

Bezier Games Werebeasts Ted Alspach and his Bezier Games companies bring us another small-box Werewolf themed game. This game shares a similar deception element, and artwork with previous releases, but like "Werewords", this is not a mainline Werewolf game or expansion.

In this game, players are auctioning off beasts of various types, and players are bidding on these creatures, whether they truly want them or not. This is because one major mechanic of the game is calling other players out on collecting specific types of creatures - if you are correct that they are hoarding a specific creature-type, then they are punished

Ultimately, this game did not appeal to us. It has a learning curve to playing, but once you get the hang of it, it makes the game feel a little too random. No matter what you really want, you need to either make a large number of offers, or make remarkable guesses about which goals other players have. Both are legitimate ways to win, but like a more standard "classic" board game, there is a definite strategy that you want to use, and there isn't a lot of replayability in this one for our group.

In our group, the only player who really liked it was the winner, and even she wasn't entirely sold on this one. It's fast, and simple, but it's a little too easy to make guesses on what other players want, and the artwork is strange.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werebeasts

text_fidelity_a:
4M Tin Can Edge Detector Robot - DIY Science Construction Stem Toy For Kids & Teens My kids like their science, particularly my youngest who envisions, among other things, working for the government and taking part in the first mission to Mars. So, given my kids interest in all things scientific, the Tin Can Edge Detector looked like something they would enjoy building and examining from a scientific point of view.

Putting this little machine together takes some effort and one reason it takes more work than it should is the instructions. They are not written as clearly as they should be. It would not have been that difficult for the manufacturer to get this right, but it seems they put little effort into it. You have to supply your own battery and a can, but most importantly, you have to be patient and give it time. It’s also best to have an adult take charge, as young children will grow frustrated if they attempt this on their own.

Once assembled, you just place the robot on a table and let it do its thing. As expected, it moves across the surface until it detects an edge, then it reverses itself. It seemed to have no trouble doing what it claimed, and that is detecting when it reached the table’s edge and not falling off. In that respect, the robot functions as it should.

Now, what about the science? Well, It can teach a little bit about robotics, but that is about the extent of the educational value. There isn’t much else to it. Oh, and green advocates will like that it requires you to provide your own soda can because it encourages recycling

Science is a popular subject with my kids but they had a difficult time getting fired up over the Tin Can Edge Detector. The problem, from a kid’s perspective, is that it doesn’t really do enough to make it interesting. Simply crawling around on a table and not falling off just didn’t cut it for my kids. Adults will dislike the assembly more than anything and the limited educational value is also a drawback. Still, it does offer kids and parents an excuse to spend a little time together and it does what the manufacturer claims, so I’m going to give it a middle rating and a passing grade. There are better educational toys, but there is enough here to keep kids semi- interested for a low price.
text_fidelity_b: 4M Tin Can Edge Detector Robot - DIY Science Construction Stem Toy For Kids & Teens

NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version I've used a LOT of drones, from professional DJI models to the cheap pocket sized tiny drones. I love flying the little ones around the house and practicing zipping in between banisters and over bookcases, and I love flying my larger DJI Phantoms and Mavic outside for real shots of landscapes and aerial photography. I was hoping this would be a good in-between product.
It is not really.
It looks a lot like the Mavic Mini, but that immediately falls apart when you hold it and realize how cheap the construction is. That's ok, it costs about 1/3 of what I paid for my Mavic Mini. But I've held cheaper drones that felt better than this. The controls are very much like the cheaper smaller drones that have been around for years (including the flip feature, which is admittedly fun), and the quality of the camera has not improved since the first cheap one I tried 5-6 years ago. Find the most basic/free cell phone you can buy from a store shelf a few years ago and the camera quality will look better than this. That was ok back then, especially since I recall paying 40-60 dollars for those drones and the cheapest DJI was closer to 800! But now, I was expecting better. At this price tag and with 2022 tech, I was hoping it would be some sort of bridge-gap product.
The downside to being larger is that it sort of doesn't fit into either category... Unlike a more expensive drone with GPS and fine tuned motors, it does not handle itself well outdoors unless there is ZERO wind (nearly impossible, especially as you climb altitude), and it is too big to fly indoors without being in danger of hitting something and actually doing damage (unlike the smaller cheaper ones). I actually can't think of a situation that I'd like to use this with: I'd recommend a smaller camera drone to play with indoors and once you are approaching the triple digit dollar amount, I'd recommend even a used Mavic Mini for outdoor flying (much more stable with GPS, and a stabilized go-pro quality camera etc).
It does come with two batteries which is nice since they go quickly, and the carrying case is pretty nice too. I guess if you're in the market for a drone like this, it DOES work so it deserves at least 3 stars, but I'm slightly disappointed with what you get for the asking price.
text_fidelity_b: NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 20 cars is too much at once. Nope! It is wonderful.

Days as a five year-old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 20 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 20 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels 20-Car Gift Pack."

Anthony Trendl
AmericanSpeechwriter.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary)

They are more portable in that you don't have to always carry a pencil sharpener or worry about emptying shavings. text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game If the classic game of Monopoly seemed to take too long, then you will appreciate this newer, shorter version. Instead of B&O Railroad, it is updated with businesses and brands like Spotify, ebay, Intel, Xbox, McDonalds and Coke. Instead of zipping around the board with an iron or a dog, you have a choice of a gold token like a coke bottle, game control, French fries, and motorcycle among others.

You choose your token, roll the dice and start buying brands, add brands to your tower, and buy and trade and take over brands with empire cards. First to the top of the tower wins. The game board reminds me of Times Square in appearance a bit.

Contents include: 4 towers for up to four players, 6 tokens, 30 billboard tiles, 6 office tiles, 14 chance cards, 14 empire cards, money pack, 2 dice and the game guide. I like this shorter, express version. I used to call the classic version Monotony, partially because my brother always beat me at it because I virtuously would save all of my $$$ and he would spend his buying up all of the real estate in the first half of the game. In the second half, I would just go around the board and pay him rent for hours on end until I ran out of $$$. Not a good strategy on my part.

I think this new version will be a hit for families who want a quick, fun game for family game night. It has current, relevant brands which is fun. And not all of the brands are about material consumption: there's ebay which is great for selling and recycling, and spotify which is about listening to good music for free - although they may charge a nominal price down the road.

While it involves luck more than strategy, some of my favorite games as a child involved luck: Chutes and Ladders, Candyland, Parcheesi etc. This is just a fun, light game for families to enjoy. When my son comes home for the weekend - he was a board game designer and now video game designer - will get his opinion and let you know what he thinks.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Dinosaurs, Dinosaur Toy, Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls 4-12 years old, Tyrannosaurus Rex, Green, 11.2" x 5.6" x 3.8" This is an impressive dinosaur figure. My son has been a long time Schleich fan, but we have had discussions several times that Papo makes a much better dinosaur than Schleich. Papo's main advantage was that they created articulated, detailed replicas of the dinosaurs of Jurassic Park. Schleich's tended to be static, less detailed and just generally clumsier reproductions. This has drastically changed with this new series of dinosaurs.

The addition of the moveable jaw and finer details has really brought the Schleich dino line up several notches. We still favor the Papos but the details in the facial features on this T Rex are great. The Jaw action is good, but the teeth are a still a little crude in their molding. The body position is gook, coloration is somewhat bold with the tannish scales. But all in all this is a great figure. Definitely a figure deserving of the Schleich tag.

Probably still second best to Papo's two T Rex figures, but heads and shoulders above the older Schleich offerings.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Dinosaurs, Dinosaur Toy, Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls 4-12 years old, Tyrannosaurus Rex, Green, 11.2" x 5.6" x 3.8"

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Toy Car Track Set Hill Climb Champion with 1:64 Scale Car, Launch Uphill to Score Points & Win Amazon was temporarily out of stock so I grabbed this from another source. We are an avid Hot Wheels family and always like to check out the newer sets. I love the idea of running a car around a course continuously, without relying on batteries. This set comes with a big launcher, that features a unique track with protruding tabs that catch the cars from behind as you blast them around the track. The whole idea is to catch the car(s) at the right time when it reenters the launcher, so you can have it racing around the course non-stop. Unfortunately, the course is too small and uninteresting, yet, if the layout was much larger, that launcher wouldn't have enough force without some kind of midway helper (like an automatic loop launcher). This would make a world of a difference in fun, so you you're not pounding the launcher every half second to keep the car circulating around a tiny oval which gets old fast.

Big annoyance: The launcher is very tall, so it comes in packed in two pieces which easily lock together, however, once locked, you're unable to seperate them. This is now the second set we have with this annoying problem. We like storing our hot wheels in their boxes, but once opened, there's no way to get this giant launcher back inside. Even if storing out of the box, with other toys, it's a big jalopy that could have been dismantled, taking up less space.

And finally, kids need laser-sharp hand/eye coordination to catch the car on time, so this may frustrate the impatient type. When you do manage to catch the car to keep it going, it does feel rewarding, even if it's only 2 laps. We haven't tried more than one car at a time, but I imagine on a large course, it must be fun, but on this small circuit, it's probably near impossible to work with.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Toy Car Track Set Hill Climb Champion with 1:64 Scale Car, Launch Uphill to Score Points & Win

text_fidelity_a:
UCanaan BJD Dolls 1/4 SD Doll 18 Inch 18 Ball Jointed Doll DIY Toys with Full Set Clothes Shoes Wig Makeup, Best Gift for Girls I absolutely love dolls of all types and own hundreds of them. They range from inexpensive off-brand play dolls, legitimate BJDs, to high-end handmade artist dolls. This is likely the worst designed doll I have ever handled.

This doll has a very cute face and poses well. However, the deal-breaker is that she has No Neck! Her head sits right on her shoulders. This is very distracting because it makes it hard to look at her. I would be able to overlook so many of the other negative aspects to this doll if she had a neck like the doll in the description photos. This is very disappointing. It's such a pity as she has a very pretty face.

This is not a BJD (ball-jointed doll). This doll shares a similar aesthetic to some BJDs, but she does not have even a single ball joint. She has hinge and swivel joints only. The doll is made from at least three different types of plastic. One maybe ABS plastic, but there are no silicone components to this doll.

Her hair is pretty rooted plugs. The description led me to believe it may be a wig, but no. The plugs are evenly spaced and I do not see any bald spots. The hair fibers are soft. The eyelashes are glued strips and the eyes are inset acrylics. She has very pretty face that is painted symmetrically. The joints were very, very stiff and difficult to loosen with force. Once loosened, she does pose decently and can touch her face. She has a full outfit that is made with flawed fabric. Several threads are missing in the weave of the fabric of the skirt. The flawed fabric is very noticeable. The outfit has a shirt, vest, skirt, bloomers, knee socks and a hat. It would be a very cute outfit if the stitching was a little more straight and the fabric was not deeply flawed fabric. The material is incredibly low quality. Her shoes are light purple canvas, do not match the outfit, but are fair quality and fit her flat feet snugly.

A packet of 'accessories' are included and is confusing. They are thin plastic, various shades of pink and not to scale with the doll. The comb and 4 little hair elastics may be useful to play with the doll but otherwise they would likely not be much fun for playing with the doll and I feel would be better left out of the package. Some heeled shoes were also included in the packet and although I could put them on the doll, the straps were useless and they looked odd as she has flat feet. Little fingers would likely become frustrated trying to fasten the straps.

I looked into the UCanaan brand after ordering this doll. I was disappointed to learn that the company uses re-casted parts from legitimate BJD makers without permission. This is very sad/bad news. I would have expected better from a US retail site and find it deeply disappointing. I do not know that any pieces are made from the re-casted parts from other companies for this particular doll, but it's a serious negative point that should be noted. I cannot say with confidence this is not a re-casted doll. I would not be surprised to learn that it is.

I cannot recommend this doll. The primary reasons being she has no neck, is not as described and the company does shady business practices. This makes me very uneasy as it sets up customers for some serious disappointment. If you are looking for a budget-friendly legitimate BJD, there are other companies that make very nice lower-cost dolls. It takes a minimum amount of looking off the site to find them. If you are looking for a nice doll for display, or posing and play, please note this one has no neck and uses poor quality materials. Your money would be better spent elsewhere. I do not find this to be a good value in the least. She would be enjoyable for display if she had a neck like the doll in the description photos. I hope that this can be remedied in the future. I find this doll very disappointing and it's such a pity as she would otherwise be very cute with an alternative outfit.

I do hope you have found my honest review helpful. If you do, please click the Helpful button below. Thank you for reading my review.
text_fidelity_b: UCanaan BJD Dolls 1/4 SD Doll 18 Inch 18 Ball Jointed Doll DIY Toys with Full Set Clothes Shoes Wig Makeup, Best Gift for Girls

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Silver There have been a number of games based on the the concept of the Golf card game. Like that game, the point of this game is to have the lowest amount of points in your hand while having a number of blind cards that may be high or low. So you need to replace them while possibly and accidentally passing a great card to the next player in the discard pile. Much like Golf, once you think you have the best hand, you call and end to the game and everyone gets one more round to try to improve them hands. If you are lowest, you get zero points, if you are not, you take a penalty.

So that is the basic idea behind the game, but from there, there are many twists to make the game more interesting. Each card has a secret ability to allow you to see the other card in your village (hand.) Also, there is a mechanism to remove duplicate cards which allows you to quickly dump a lot of points from your hand (village.)

The cards are very nice, the amulet is also nice and allows you to lock a great card so that neither you or others can mess with it. The box could be a lot smaller, basically this is a deck game with a single piece for locking a card. you could put it into a box for a pack of hoyles cards.

All in all, an interesting twist on a classic card game concept.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Silver

text_fidelity_a: Barbie Splish Splash Pup Playset My almost 4 year old is just starting to take an interest in Barbies. I'm so mad I didn't keep all of mine from my childhood, I could be saving a bundle!  She really doesn't care what Barbie she gets, she just loves to use her imagination and play with dolls. We had a small birthday party for her at my Grandparents house since they cannot travel to come to her main birthday party.  We bought her a Power Wheels for her birthday, so I didn't want to spend a lot but needed something to give her at her "other" party. I am so glad I went with this!  Her and her 2 cousins (7 year old girl and 3 year old boy) had so much fun playing with this set.  When I was taking it out of the box and talking to my daughter about the dog shaking the water off my Mom kept saying there's no way that dog is going to move. We were all pleasantly surprised when I pushed down on the dog colar. I LOVE that there are no batteries, no winding it up, just push down and watch the dogs tail spin in circles and head go back and forth. I read several reviews that love the dog, but were dissappointed in the barbie.  I knew going in that her arms don't move from their position, so I wasn't thrown off by that feature, and I honestly don't think it's a big deal AT ALL. The kids didn't seem to mind one bit. The thing is, there are a million different barbies, that do a million different things. This Barbie is the designated dog washer in Barbie Land, lol. Her arms don't need to move for her to serve her purpose... Of course anything with water is going to hold a childs attention just a little bit longer than usual. The three kids sat on the bathroom floor for over an hour taking turns washing the dog!  Their favorite feature is the soap bottle. I will say that is the only thing that may become annoying to a parent over time. It's appropriately sized for the playset, but we found ourselves refilling that bottle about every 4-5 minutes while they played with it. If you have an older child who could fill it themselves with water and a drop or two of soap, then you have nothing to worry about. The soap bottle is actually a really ingenius feature. I filled it with water and added about a quarter pump of hand soap, put the cap back on and shook it up before giving it back to the kids. If you hold it upside down (cap side down) water comes out the holes, but if you hold it right side up (or sideways) and squeeze you'll only have bubbles coming out so you can "wash" the dog. This is hands down her favorite Barbie in her collection! Such a simple concept, yet it's provided hours of fun every day for the past week.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Splish Splash Pup Playset

That one, grips onto our lawn and has a lot of power for going up and down the small hills in our grassy yard.

This one, seems to even have more power than our last one, but unfortunately the tires are less grippy, so it ends up spinning out and people get stuck trying to go up a hill and have to strategize about what long and circuitous route they can take to get up the hill kind of sideways so that it doesn't lose power or more usually, spin its wheels.

This thing goes a bit faster than our other one, and has a feel of power to it, so I really think the wheels and their slippery, hard surface, are the issue. This is gotten slightly better with use over the last few months, but unfortunately is still happening very frequently when in use. We have found the issue is just as bad on our concrete driveway as it is on our grass. Our grass is a bumpy, country lawn that is generally on watered in summer and goes kind of brown and dry.

I also think they could've improved it by potentially making it big enough to seat a second, smaller child. Our other one is big enough that when our son was five and our daughter was three, she could sit behind him as he drove around the yard.

Overall, if you have a very flat, large lawn that a child would be unlikely to spin out the tires on, this is a really fun, immediately thrilling toy to play with, has a ton of power, multiple settings that are fun for the kids to experiment with, and is very maneuverable and controllable. However, for bumpier lawns or yards with some minor grade changes and hills, this might not be the best choice for getting around.
text_fidelity_b: Pink Racer

text_fidelity_a:
Blue Orange Flash! Lightening Fast Party Family Dice Rolling Game Games, for 2-6 Players, Ages 7+ Flash is a simple yet fun dice game for the entire family. It consists of six sets of six dice, each distinguished by a different color, six numbered chips for scoring, a score pad with eight challenges and a small pencil, and a storage bag and instructions.

Flash is a fast game and this is one of the reasons busy parents and others will enjoy playing it so much. The object of the game is to complete each of the eight challenges faster than your opponents and what makes it move so quickly is that everyone plays at the same time, racing against each other to see who can complete the challenge the most quickly. Unlike Yahtzee and other dice games where each person plays solo while the others wait, this game offers all- out action through each challenge.

What are the challenges in Flash? Well, they are basic numbering combinations such as six of a kind, a straight, etc. It sounds like it might be difficult, but it really isn't because each individual die has a flash (lightning bolt) on one side that counts as a wildcard. All you do is throw your dice, keep the ones that you need, then pick up the other dice and throw them again and again until you meet the challenge. Whoever completes it first yells "Flash" and picks up the highest scoring chip. Everyone else keeps throwing the dice until they get the challenge correct, but they get a lower scoring chip, all the way down to the number 1 chip. Play continues through all of the challenges and the highest scoring player wins.

The simplicity of this game is one of its strongest points and kids seem to like it more than a game such as Yahtzee for several reasons. First, the speed- it's an all- out battle to see who can meet the challenge before anyone else. Second, every challenge is certain to be met, in contrast with Yahtzee where you may or may not be able to complete each of the items on the score sheet. The scoring is simpler, too, and I like that the manufacturer included a small bag in which to place the dice, chips, pencil, and scoring pad because they would eventually get lost without it.

If I had to look for something to criticize with this dice game, it would be the fact that the challenges are really not that challenging. No matter how bad your luck may be, you will be able to complete each and every challenge- usually in two minutes max. It is only a matter of time until you roll the right numbers on the dice and the wildcard flash makes each challenge that much easier to achieve.

Family game night is part of growing up and Flash is a good game to have around on those nights when you want some family entertainment and only have about 20 minutes or less to spare. It's a fun little game that most anyone will find worthwhile and worth playing.
text_fidelity_b: Blue Orange Flash! Lightening Fast Party Family Dice Rolling Game Games, for 2-6 Players, Ages 7+

Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. Okay, so I got the kit and made the TWO potholders. I bought this kit because the loom was metal, and I'd read reviews and seen videos where the person's PLASTIC loom would break. So, what's the problem?
I really don't like how the loops slip off this loom, especially when you're getting towards completing the project. Pop, pop, pop go the loops - OFF the loom! This might be the nature of pot-holder looming, but I think the problem is the little spokes (hooks) are straight, so there's nothing to keep the loops from slipping off. They should be curved and WIDER at the top so the loops can't slide off. Towards the end, when you're crocheting the edges together, the last side can get completely unraveled.
THAT IS frustrating.
I'm going to try to find another loom.
Unfortunately, I looked at a lot looms before I bought this one, and they ALL seem to have the same design flaw.

Afterthought:
On a positive note: the loops are NOT polyester, but cotton, so the potholders came out nice 'n thick and heavy.
I can see why posters said they lasted a long time. They probably will.
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs.
